# <span id="aanchor414"></span> Transaction Queue Extraction

The TQ Extraction utility allows users to connect to a FLOWCAL database and extract Transaction Queue data in the form of text files containing SQL statements that can then be shared with support staff.

This data can then be used to troubleshoot issues or reproduce and test activities related to transaction processing or the data in question.

<div class="procedure">

## Running TQ Extraction

The TQ Extraction utility contains a single self-contained executable (TQRecExtraction.exe). To run the TQ Extraction utility:

1.  Copy the executable into the FLOWCAL Installation folder containing the flowcal.exe file.

2.  Double-click the **TQRecExtraction.exe** file.

3.  Enter a FLOWCAL user name, password and database name.

    

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 188;height: 118;" />

4.  Select the object type (Meter, Source, or Tickets) for which data will be extracted.

5.  Select the object number from the drop-down box in the top left corner.

6.  Use the **From** and **To** fields to designate a date range.

7.  Configure the remaining options as needed:
    - **All Gas Transactions** – When this is checked, all gas transactions will be extracted and saved as a single SQL file. The From and To dates are still used to limit the time frame.
    - **All Liquid Transactions** – When this is checked, all liquid transactions will be extracted and saved as a single SQL file. The From and To dates are still used to limit the time frame.
    - **Unprocessed Records Only** – This option, when selected in conjunction with any of the other extract options, will only allow for the extraction of records that have not been processed. For gas records this means that FC_TRANSACTION_QUEUE.UNAVAILABLE = 0 and for liquid transactions FC_TQ_MANAGER.STATUS = 0.
    - **Source ID** - The utility will extract all transactions with a specific source ID and ignore the object number.

    <!-- -->

    - 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 322;height: 372;" />

Upon completion of the extraction, the utility will create the following SQL text files:

- For meter data, there will be two files with the following naming format:

  \_TQ_Recs_Meter\_\<Meter Number or TQ Source ID\>.sql

  \_TQ_Snapshot_Recs_Meter\_\<Meter Number or TQ Source ID\>.sql

- For quality source data, there will be a single file with the following naming format:

  \_TQ_Recs_GQ\_\<Quality Source Number or TQ Source ID\>.sql

These SQL files can then be shared with support staff, along with FcDabaBoss transfers for the purposes mentioned above.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Meter Transactions">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Export Meter Transactions</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Meter Transactions">

To export meter transactions, the ‘Meter’ radio button must be selected. The drop-down list will be populated with all available gas and liquid meter numbers. This does not take into account a user’s security permissions. A meter may be selected from the list or a source id may be provided in the ‘Source ID’ text box. The ‘From’ and ‘To’ date may be adjusted to fit the time span of the data that is being extracted. Populating Source ID will override the meter number selection from the drop-down. The Source ID is used if there is a source ID to be extracted that does not match a meter number in the database. This would be the case if auto creating a meter or if importing by Source ID rather than meter number.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 316;height: 365;" />

When the tool is run, messages will populate the application window that show the number of transactions that are being extracted. Those extracted transactions are formatted into insert statements and saved as a SQL file in the same location as the TQ Extraction Tool.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 320;height: 368;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Source Transactions">

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Source Transactions">

To export source analyses transactions, the ‘Source’ radio button must be selected. The drop-down list will be populated with all available gas and liquid quality source numbers. This does not take into account a user’s security permissions. A source may be selected from the list or a source id may be provided in the ‘Source ID’ text box. The ‘From’ and ‘To’ date may be adjusted to fit the time span of the data that is being extracted. Populating Source ID will override the quality source number selection from the drop-down. The Source ID is used if there is a source ID to be extracted that does not match a quality source number in the database. This would be the case if auto creating a quality source or if importing by Source ID rather than source number.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 326;height: 376;" />

When the tool is run, messages will populate the application window that show the number of transactions that are being extracted. Those extracted transactions are formatted into insert statements and saved as a SQL file in the same location as the TQ Extraction Tool.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Ticket Transactions">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Export Ticket Transactions</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Ticket Transactions">

To export Ticket transactions, the ‘Tickets’ radio button must be selected. The drop-down list will be populated will all available locations that can have a ticket attached to it. Comparison locations, for example, will not be in the drop-down. A location may be selected from the drop-down or a source id for the specific ticket may be provided in the ‘Source ID’ text box. The ‘From’ and ‘To’ date may be adjusted to fit the time span of the data that is being extracted.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 326;height: 376;" />

When the tool is run, messages will populate the application window that show the number of transactions that are being extracted. Those extracted transactions are formatted into insert statements and saved as a SQL file in the same location as the TQ Extraction Tool.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Standalone">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Export Standalone Tickets and Sample Analyses</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Standalone">

Standalone Tickets and Sample Analysis records exist independently of any quality source or location. To extract these transactions, the user needs to enter the specific source id into the ‘Source ID” field in the extraction tool and select the appropriate date range.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 326;height: 376;" />

When the tool is run, messages will populate the application window that show the number of transactions that are being extracted. Those extracted transactions are formatted into insert statements and saved as a SQL file in the same location as the TQ Extraction Tool.

</div>
